findings.text: SMP dispatch table smp_ops binds boot preparation, application processor preparation and completion, peer shutdown, reschedule signalling, liveness kick, disable and idle handling, plus broadcast and single-target function-call IPIs, to native routines, with a separate crash path when dump support is enabled.
Handler sysvec_reboot acknowledges the local interrupt, tears down virtualization in emergency mode on this CPU, then parks the CPU through the shared stop path.

Peer shutdown in native_stop_other_cpus elects a single initiator with an atomic compare on stopping_cpu, returns immediately when reboot_force is set, and first calls smp_kick_mwait_play_dead when kexec_in_progress is set. The winner builds cpus_stop_mask from online CPUs minus itself, broadcasts REBOOT_VECTOR, then polls roughly one second for the mask to drain.

If the mask remains nonempty, native_stop_other_cpus optionally registers a first NMI stop callback via register_stop_handler unless smp_no_nmi_ipi is set, sends NMI_VECTOR to each listed CPU, logs an emergency notice, then waits up to ten milliseconds or forever when wait was requested. It then saves flags, disables the local APIC, clears machine-check state, restores flags and clears cpus_stop_mask to push invalidations to peers.

Peer shutdown cannot avoid interrupting CPUs that still hold locks, cannot prevent a late CPU from reporting halt after the NMI decision was taken, and cannot stop disabled APICs from reacting to NMI, so completion of the mask does not prove every target finished its NMI handler.

Handlers sysvec_reschedule_ipi, sysvec_call_function and sysvec_call_function_single each acknowledge the interrupt and account the event with tracing, then dispatch respectively to the scheduler wakeup path, the generic broadcast function path, or the generic single-target function path for RESCHEDULE_VECTOR, CALL_FUNCTION_VECTOR and CALL_FUNCTION_SINGLE_VECTOR.
Early parameter handler nonmi_ipi_setup sets smp_no_nmi_ipi to disable the NMI shutdown fallback and returns success.
Record mwait_cpu_dead carries two unsigned handshake words named control and status, written by both the parked CPU and the controller to coordinate exit from monitor-wait toward halt.
Handshake waiting marker CPUDEAD_MWAIT_WAIT equals hexadecimal DEADBEEF and kexec halt marker CPUDEAD_MWAIT_KEXEC_HLT equals hexadecimal 4A17DEAD.

Routine smp_kick_mwait_play_dead scans present but offline CPUs, reads each per-CPU mwait_cpu_dead status once, skips CPUs not showing CPUDEAD_MWAIT_WAIT, otherwise writes CPUDEAD_MWAIT_KEXEC_HLT into control and rechecks with short delays for about five milliseconds, reporting once when a CPU stays stuck.
Topology state holds per-CPU read-mostly sharing masks cpu_sibling_map, cpu_core_map and cpu_die_map plus a global cpu_sibling_setup_mask recording which CPUs already built sibling state.

Global __max_smt_threads defaults to one, and boolean x86_topology_update signals pending topology refresh consumed exactly once by arch_update_cpu_topology which returns the prior value and clears the flag.

Warm-reset vector programming in smpboot_setup_warm_reset_vector and teardown in smpboot_restore_warm_reset_vector share counter smpboot_warm_reset_vector_count under rtc_lock with interrupts saved. First setup writes shutdown code ten and a segmented start address split for TRAMPOLINE_PHYS_HIGH and TRAMPOLINE_PHYS_LOW; last restore writes shutdown code zero and clears the word at TRAMPOLINE_PHYS_LOW.

Routine ap_starting zeroes local mwait_cpu_dead control and status, brings up the local APIC, identifies the CPU, builds sibling state before announcing start with a write barrier, initializes aperf counters and announces start. Helper ap_calibrate_delay refreshes the per-CPU loop speed estimate from the calibrated delay loop, skipping work when the counter is already known synchronized.

Entry start_secondary orders bringup as control-register init, 32-bit page-table switch with full flush, exception setup without end-branch, early microcode load, alive handshake with the controller, core and floating-point init, read-copy-update and clock announces, ap_starting, TSC sync check via check_tsc_sync_target, delay calibration via ap_calibrate_delay, store-bypass sibling init, then under vector_lock mark online plus local vector bringup, NMI init, enable interrupts, per-CPU clockevent setup and idle entry with a write barrier beforehand.

Loading microcode before the alive handshake keeps parallel bringup fast and relies on primary threads preceding secondary threads, but concurrent loads on threading siblings that alter identification state remain unsafe and must be serialized outside this path, as must any load changing identification or model-specific state observed by software.
Transition to online must hold vector_lock across marking the CPU online and bringing its vector allocator online so peers configuring interrupts never see a partially constructed vector allocation.

Target check_tsc_sync_target skips when the unsynchronized predicate reports true, when adjustment validation succeeds, or when the reliable clock property holds. Otherwise it delegates measurement to the first online CPU, joins a two-party start barrier, measures via check_tsc_warp, joins a stop barrier, and on remaining test runs adjusts per-CPU compensation by observed warp with sign fix for the ahead case, programs MSR_IA32_TSC_ADJUST and retries.

Predicate unsynchronized_tsc reports unsynchronized when the counter feature is missing or flagged unstable, or under clustered interrupt topology, but reports synchronized when constant or reliable properties hold. On non-Intel vendors it treats multi-package systems as unsynchronized and otherwise assumes synchronization.

Warp detector check_tsc_warp samples the ordered counter under a global spin lock against a shared last value, runs until a deadline or a large iteration cap with periodic relax and watchdog touches, warns on zero progress, records the largest backward step globally and counts how many CPUs observed warps to flag bouncing, returning the caller-observed maximum.

Shared warp state and last timestamp are protected by spin lock sync_lock held only around sampling and around updates to maximum warp and warp counters, with backward detection itself performed outside the critical section.
Warp measurement duration from loop_timeout is short when the calling core hosts more than one thread and longer for single-threaded cores.

Scheduler hierarchy x86_topology exposes thread, optional cluster, optional multi-core and package levels with flag helpers x86_sched_itmt_flags, x86_core_flags and x86_cluster_flags adding asymmetric-packing preference when the imbalance-tolerance control is enabled; builder build_sched_topology removes the package level when a package spans multiple NUMA nodes and skips the thread level when only one thread per core exists.

NUMA distance query arch_sched_node_distance returns the base firmware distance except on INTEL_GRANITERAPIDS_X and INTEL_ATOM_DARKMONT_X with multiple packages and at least three nodes per package, where off-trace sub-NUMA cluster distances from slit_cluster_distance are repaired by averaging both directions over paired clusters after one-time validation via slit_validate that on-trace clusters are symmetric via slit_cluster_symmetric and map to distinct packages via slit_cluster_package; validation failure logs a firmware issue and falls back to base distances.
Legacy init delay constant UDELAY_10MS_LEGACY equals ten thousand microseconds and configurable init_udelay defaults to the maximum unsigned integer until a boot option overrides it.
Early boot handlers split_llc_setup and cpu_init_udelay each parse an unsigned integer respectively into split_llc defaulting to zero and into init_udelay.
Cluster identification table intel_cod_cpu matches INTEL_HASWELL_X and INTEL_BROADWELL_X server types as cluster mode, treats INTEL_ANY as sub-NUMA-cluster mode, and terminates with an empty entry.
Helpers cpu_coregroup_mask and cpu_clustergroup_mask delegate respectively to the shared last-level-cache mask and the shared second-level-cache mask.

Rescan arch_cpu_rescan_dead_smt_siblings is a no-op unless threading was disabled or force-disabled; otherwise it transiently re-enables then re-disables threading under hotplug to migrate siblings parked in halt into monitor-wait, propagating any failure.
After bringup impress_friends sums per-CPU loop speed estimates over online CPUs and logs total processor count with aggregate speed.

INIT sequence send_init_sequence clears interrupt-controller errors on integrated versions including a legacy erratum workaround, asserts level-triggered INIT to the target physical identifier, waits for bus idle, delays by init_udelay, then deasserts INIT and again waits for idle.
Diagnostic prefix pr_fmt prepends the module name to every formatted message in this file.
